title: Watch Me Walk by Anne Gridley at Soho Rep #watchmewalk #sohorep #utrf...
transcript: Watch Me Walk by Anne Gridley is a messy and deeply personal portrait of grief and disability — but it's not a complete wash of despair. In direct address to the audience, Anne spends much of the show explaining how she experiences life with hereditary spastic paraplegia, a genetic condition that poses significant mobility challenges. Something that comes up in the play a few times is that the symptoms of this disorder didn't present themselves until Anne was an adult. This opens up an interesting dimension of grief for the mobility that she used to have, and it positions her in a way where she can speak to how the world treats you when you're disabled versus when you're not. It's a lot to carry, and a lot to digest as an audience member, but she sprinkles in a charmingly wry and dark humor that I think balances the tone of the piece quite nicely. Unfortunately, the focus definitely frays in the latter half — there's still plenty of interesting material, such as some insane family lore and musical musings on internalized ableism, but it doesn't quite come together for me. I felt it overstated its welcome and couldn't make a strong enough case for what the takeaway is, though in fairness, it may not intend to declare just one. With that, another program for my collection.
